corrections.source_says: GPTZero, the commercial detector whose labels define the AI-use measure in every main result, gave the authors free API access. Set any to true and describe it as in-kind support (free API access) from GPTZero. The paper also cites GPTZero's own technical report [22] for the detector's error rate.
corrections.quote: We thank the admissions staff at our partner institution for data access and guidance, GPTZero for providing free API access, and Alex Adam for helpful conversations.
corrections.locator: p. 1, Acknowledgments; p. 3, Section 3.1 and p. 12, ref. [22]

corrections.form_value: In 7,462 applications to a public policy master's program, 56.1% of 2025 applicants submitted at least one GPTZero-flagged AI essay (p. 30, Table A1). LLM-scored essay quality rose after ChatGPT (figure only, p. 6, Fig. 3). Each AI-flagged essay lowered admission by 1.5 p.p. (DML -0.015, SE 0.006; p. 7, Table 1).
corrections.source_says: Two problems. (a) The admission models use only the 2023 and 2024 cycles (p. 22, Appendix D), and 2025 outcomes are not analyzed (p. 6, fn. 4), so the 1.5 p.p. estimate does not cover the 7,462 applications. The authors call it an 'apparent penalty' that unmeasured confounding may affect, so 'lowered' overstates it. (b) The form spec asks for one sentence, and the field has three. Suggested: 'In 7,462 applications (2020-2025) to a U.S. public policy master's program, 56.1% of 2025 applicants submitted at least one GPTZero-flagged AI essay (p. 30, Table A1), LLM-scored essay quality rose after ChatGPT (figure only, p. 6, Fig. 3), and in the 2023-2024 cycles each AI-flagged essay was associated with a 1.5 p.p. lower admission probability after covariate adjustment (DML -0.015, SE 0.006; p. 7, Table 1).'
corrections.quote: Finally, our estimate of the apparent penalty associated with AI use may be affected by unmeasured confounding.
corrections.locator: p. 10, Section 4; p. 6, fn. 4; p. 7, Table 1 and text; p. 22, Appendix D

corrections.form_value: ... detector and threshold robustness Tables A1, A2, A4-A7 (E)
corrections.source_says: Only Tables A5-A7 belong to the Section E robustness checks. Tables A1 and A2 (AI detection and false-positive rates by detector and threshold, at the applicant and essay level) are discussed in Appendix A.2.2-A.2.3, and Table A4 (residual variation in the AI essay count) in Appendix D. All seven tables sit at the end of the PDF, pp. 30-36.
corrections.quote: Tables A1 and A2 report the AI detection rates by year of material submission across a variety of classification thresholds, at the applicant and essay level, respectively.
corrections.locator: p. 19, A.2.2; p. 20, A.2.3; p. 23, Appendix D ('Residual variation checks') and Section E; pp. 30-36

corrections.form_value: Template strings left in place: 'yes | no | not_stated', 'individual | team | class | session | within_person_order | other', 'yes | no | mixed', 'immediate | delayed'
corrections.source_says: The paper reports IRB approval (protocol IRB24-0242) but no preregistration, so preregistered should be 'not_stated'. Nothing is assigned, so unit is best 'other'. AI availability: S1-O1 and S1-O2 compare pre-ChatGPT and post-ChatGPT essays ('mixed'), and S1-O3 and S2-O1 use 2023-2024 essays, written after ChatGPT's release when AI was available though prohibited ('yes'). Timing is 'immediate' for all four outcomes, because each score is of the essay as submitted.
corrections.quote: Starting in 2023—the first cycle after ChatGPT was released—this attestation was expanded to exclude use of generative AI.
corrections.locator: p. 3, Section 3; p. 20, Appendix B; p. 22, Appendix D

confirmed: source.version is exact: the PDF margin reads arXiv:2609.22549v1 [cs.CY] 18 Sep 2026, the PDF has 36 pages, and the arXiv API still lists v1 (published 2026-09-18) as the only version on 6 October 2026 (p. 1; arXiv API).
The title and the three authors (Calvin Isley, Johann D. Gaebler, Sharad Goel) match (p. 1).

No study randomizes people to AI. S1 compares admissions cohorts and GPTZero-flagged versus non-flagged applicants. S2 randomizes only the order in which officers read the essays and the draw of 50 matched pairs, so has_randomized_people_study is false (pp. 2-7; p. 20, Appendix B).

The design classes fit: S1 is observational (real essays compared across time and across detected adopters and non-adopters), and S2 is a perception study of how admissions officers detect and rate AI-written essays, a study type the codebook excludes, so design_class other is acceptable (pp. 3-8, 20-21; codebook Section 3).

Eligibility core no and criterion 1 not_met are correct. Context class observational is a defensible borderline call: the only originality-related outcome is the LLM-scored 'voice and originality' dimension, which appears as its own series only in Fig. A4 (p. 18, A.1.2; p. 27).

S1 counts match: 7,462 applications over six cycles, 2020-2025. The paper counts applications, not distinct applicants, and prints no N for the admission models. The S1 quote is verbatim (p. 2, Section 2; p. 15, A.1; p. 7, Table 1).
2025 admission outcomes are not analyzed because the program changed its admissions process after seeing preliminary results (p. 6, fn. 4; p. 18, A.1.4).

S2 counts match: five staff members; 100 essays from 2023-2024 (50 human, 50 AI) matched 1:1 by propensity score; Rater 1 rated 60 (32 human, 28 AI); 460 ratings in total; the 22 'very likely AI' ratings were dropped only for the weight model. The S2 quote is verbatim and 32 words long (pp. 20-21, Appendices B and C.1).

Table 2 matches cell by cell: AI Likelihood -0.131* (0.059), -0.119* (0.047), -0.109* (0.047); LLM-Based Quality 1.029*** (0.090), 0.995*** (0.093); AI-Written 0.019 (0.101), -0.033 (0.102); SEs clustered by applicant; reviewer fixed effects in all three columns (p. 10).
Table 2 prints no N. The form's 460 is the total number of ratings, which the paper prints (p. 20, Appendix B).

S2-O1 direction no_clear_difference rests on the AI-Written coefficient, which is conditional on LLM-based quality and AI likelihood. The reported string names the columns, so it is accurate (p. 10, Table 2).
56.1% (SE 1.5%) of 2025 applicants flagged by GPTZero AI-only, high-confidence labels matches Table A1, column (1) (p. 30).
S1-O1 is figure only: Fig. 3 prints no numbers, and the quoted sentence and 'more modest' are verbatim (pp. 5-6, Section 3.2, Fig. 3; p. 21, C.2).

Measure details match: seven gpt-5-mini rubric dimensions on five-point scales; weights from an OLS of officers' ratings with rater fixed effects (Table A3, Voice 0.226 [0.107, 0.346]); applicant-level averages in 2020 SD units; Fig. A4 year coefficients with applicant controls, normalized by the 2020 within-group SD, SEs clustered at the applicant level (p. 5; p. 18; p. 21, C.1-C.2; p. 27; p. 32).

Detectors match: GPTZero model 3.9 in the main analysis and Pangram 3.1 in robustness checks. Robustness Tables A5 (Pangram), A6 (thresholds and the changed-prompt essay), and A7 (binary treatment) exist as described (p. 18, A.2; p. 23; pp. 34-36).
S1-O3 measure detail matches: about 400 covariates (397 in the primary specification, 398 pooled) and 14 essay-quality measures (p. 6; p. 18, A.1.2; p. 22, Appendix D).
Essay quality and admission probability are the paper's two named primary outcomes, so paper_primary for S1-O1 and S1-O3 is correct (p. 18, A.1.4).
sample_overlap left blank is defensible: the paper says only that its data pipeline is described in concurrent work [20, 21], not that those papers analyze the same applicants (p. 15, Appendix A).
data_and_code left blank is correct: the paper gives no data or code links (full PDF).
summary: No study in c382 randomizes people to AI (S1 is observational admissions data on 7,462 applications, S2 a five-officer perception study), and the form's design calls, counts, and every number from Tables 1, 2, and A1 match the PDF. Five fixes: the Fig. A4 Voice description misreads the 2023-2024 points (international 2024 is about +0.14), company_involvement should be true because GPTZero gave free API access, the one-line finding should be one sentence that limits the 1.5 p.p. penalty to the 2023-2024 cycles as a covariate-adjusted association, the supplement entry misplaces Tables A1, A2, and A4 in Section E, and several enum fields still hold template strings.
